question: Is 'STALE at 30 days untouched' (FR-91, resolved-spec-d4000f.md:328) meant to be a new StoredWorkStatus enum member, or an orthogonal derived flag layered on top of an existing status (e.g. 'planned' + age)? I could not open src/lib/server/workitems/rules.ts in this pass to check the actual union.
guess: Treated it as out of scope for this note and recommended u4 confirm against rules.ts directly rather than guessing the shape.

question: Should the new FR-96b engagement-filter reader be added to src/lib/answer-query.ts (extending the existing shared SearchParams/parse* helpers) or to a new shared module, given that 2 of 11 screens (/runs, /registry) don't import from answer-query.ts at all today and would need to adopt it for the first time?
guess: Recommended in the note that whichever unit touches answer-query.ts first export one shared engagementFilterFrom() helper, and that /runs and /registry adopt the same SearchParams type rather than inventing a fourth shape. Did not pick which unit owns this — that's a project-lead sequencing call.

question: work_item is class `sensitive` and 7a names exactly two encrypted columns on it (description, raw_status). Should the new FR-90 reconciliation key `plan_ref` be encrypted as well?
best_guess: Left CLEAR. 7a's own pattern for a sensitive table is prose encrypted / identifiers clear, stated explicitly for requirement (text encrypted, ref and section clear) and already applied to work_item.unit. plan_ref is an identifier the plan and manifest both echo, not client prose. It is also load-bearing: an encrypted column cannot be indexed or matched, so encrypting the reconciliation key would delete the requirement it exists for. Recorded rather than assumed because 7a does not name this column by name.

question: What shape should the FR-90 collision mark take — a per-row state, or a pairwise edge naming the row it collides with?
best_guess: A per-row state (`plan_reconciliation` enum), with NO `collides_with` foreign key. Reasoning: where no shared key exists you cannot identify WHICH two rows correspond without matching prose, and Q13 excludes prose similarity absolutely. A pairwise edge would therefore have to be populated by the exact mechanism the ruling forbids. If Erik wants the pair recorded, FR-90's deferred write half is where that belongs, once artifacts actually carry the id.

question: FR-91 says a planned row 'untouched for 30 days' is STALE. Is 'untouched' the row's last modification (updated_at) or its creation (created_at)?
best_guess: updated_at, maintained by a BEFORE UPDATE trigger so no write path can forget to bump it. Both columns were added, so unit i4 can derive from either without a further migration. created_at alone would make an actively edited plan row go stale while someone is working on it.

question: Making execution_mode nullable is silent to TypeScript at four read sites. Who owns correcting them — i3, i4, u4, or a follow-up?
best_guess: NOT changed by i1, and handed to i3/u4 with exact file:line. Correcting them means widening the domain `ExecutionMode` to admit null, which cascades into three TSX components (ExecutionModeChip and its two callers) — that is ui-designer's surface, and i1 is forbidden from writing React. MEASURED, not assumed: fromExecutionMode(null) returns 'fleet', so a planned row reads as fleet work on the answer screens and both detail views; and work-items list passes the raw null through to EXECUTION_MODE_LABELS[null], which is undefined, so the chip renders blank. Both are invisible to tsc and to the 1550-test suite. This is the FR-91 misread ('nobody has started this' reading as 'in flight') and it becomes live the moment i3 writes the first planned row.

question: What syntax will the plan template emit for the explicit reconciliation id, once that template change lands outside this repo?
best_guess: A `**Plan-id:** <token>` line in the task body, matching the `**Files:**` / `**Interfaces:**` field lines the writing-plans shape already uses. Token is `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*`, optionally backticked. Parsed today; no artifact emits one, so every task returns planRef null. Changing the syntax later is a one-regex change plus one fixture.

question: Which lines inside a genuine plan document are classification candidates — i.e. which lines can become `unparsed` rows?
best_guess: Only lines that present as the shape: a heading whose text begins with the word `Task`, a bullet carrying a one-character bracket, and a `**Plan-id:**` line. Body prose and fenced code are the task's content, not candidates. Treating every prose line as a candidate would turn plan.md's 2160 lines into thousands of unparsed rows, which contradicts the Q12 ruling's own 'not a page of unparsed rows'.

question: Does one `### Task N:` heading become one work_item row, or does each `- [ ]` step become its own row?
best_guess: One row per task heading; steps ride along on the task record as structured data for i3 to use or drop. A step is a procedure inside one unit of work, not a separately dispatchable item, and 82 rows from one plan.md would drown the Next screen.

question: Should the parser be wired into the existing run-ingest path (`src/lib/ingest/ingestRun.ts`)?
best_guess: No. A plan document is not a run artifact and `RunInput` has no slot for one. i2 ships the parser unwired and unit i3 owns the seam. Flagging it explicitly because an unwired parser ships inert and looks finished.

question: Now that one engagement picker lives in the app shell, should u3 REMOVE the per-screen free-text `EngagementFilter` input that the six answer screens already carry in their filter bars, or keep both controls?
best_guess: Keep both for this run. FR-96b's 'not built eleven times' is satisfied by not adding an eleventh copy; removing six existing, tested controls is a behaviour change on six screens that FR-96b does not ask for, and the free-text field is the only way to type a slug the picker does not list. Flagged to u3 as a decision it must not make silently.

question: Should the shell picker render on screens that do NOT honour the filter — the `[id]` detail views, `/settings/*`, `/`, `/registry/new`, `/work-items/unassigned`?
best_guess: No. It renders only on the eleven paths CR-005 §3.3 point 1 names. Offering a filter where nothing honours it lets Erik set a scope that narrows nothing, which is the same lie as a screen that looks scoped while showing everything. The cost is that the control disappears when he opens a detail view; the URL is the entire state, so going back restores it.

question: Should the '(whole ledger)' scope note also appear when the unparsed count is UNKNOWN, i.e. 'unparsed count unavailable (whole ledger)'?
best_guess: No. FR-96a exists to stop a ledger-wide NUMBER being read as a scoped one, and the unknown state renders no number — there is nothing to misread. Suppressing it also protects the 375px width the short label was introduced to save. The badge still reports `data-verify-scope="none"` in that state, so an assertion can tell the two apart.

question: `pnpm gate:m27:e2e` cannot be run from a fleet worktree: it needs an instance carrying real rows, and a worktree has no `.env.local` (read-denied by design, and the copy was refused by the permission system). Who runs it, and when?
best_guess: The orchestrator runs it from the merged shared checkout after fan-in, with both env vars set. This unit reports it NOT VERIFIED rather than running it against the shared checkout's server, which would be testing another tree's code and reporting it as this unit's pass.

question: Is a planned row untouched for EXACTLY 30 days STALE, or does it become STALE only on day 31?
best_guess: Inclusive: >= 30 days is STALE. 'Untouched for 30 days' is true at thirty days, and a boundary left to the reader is a boundary two callers implement two ways. Stated once as PLANNED_STALE_AFTER_DAYS and tested at 29/30/31.

question: Is the 30-day age measured in whole UTC calendar days (truncating updated_at to its day) or in elapsed instants (30 x 24h)?
best_guess: Whole UTC calendar days, via toIsoDay + daysBetween, which is the only whole-day arithmetic this repo has and what every other elapsed count uses. Consequence: a row touched at 23:59Z and one touched at 00:01Z on the same date are the same age, so a row can surface STALE up to ~24h 'early' against an instant reading. Surfacing early is the conservative direction for a signal that deletes nothing.

question: How should a planned row whose updated_at cannot be read surface — the derivation returns state 'unknown' rather than guessing fresh or stale, and u4 needs a treatment for it.
best_guess: Render it distinctly from both PLANNED-fresh and PLANNED-STALE (the unparsed discipline applied to a date: never a guess). It should be unreachable in practice — updated_at is NOT NULL DEFAULT now() behind i1's BEFORE UPDATE trigger — so a visible 'age unknown' is a real finding about a read path, not noise.

question: Does a STALE planned row change its behaviour on Next (FR-53) — reordered, demoted, or excluded — or is STALE purely a visual mark?
best_guess: Purely a visual mark. FR-91 says 'surfaces as STALE' and Q15 says 'surfaced and never deleted'; nothing says the row leaves Next or moves within it. This unit changed no ordering and no inclusion rule, and Next's ordering stays FR-53's nearest-dated-milestone.

question: May planned work be created against an ARCHIVED engagement? The picker already excludes archived engagements (u1's readEngagementRoster filters archivedAt === null), but the shared insert primitive does not, so a slug naming an archived engagement still resolves for i3's plan-document path and for any hand-made request.
best_guess: Do not refuse it in the primitive. CR-005 states no such rule and the picker already keeps it out of the hand-entry path; adding a refusal here would be a rule invented in a work-unit rather than declared in the spec, and it would silently break replanning against an engagement Erik tidied away and then reopened.

question: Should the FR-88 hand-entry form let Erik set executor_kind, in particular 'erik_gate'? A planned item only Erik can do is invisible to /bottleneck's erik_gate count until it is dispatched.
best_guess: No. The primitive forces executor_kind = 'unassigned' and the form offers no control. FR-87 defines planned work as undispatched, and letting a planned row claim an executor before anyone agreed to it is the same class of claim as a wrong 'done'. Revisit if /bottleneck is expected to answer for planned work.

question: For i3's plan-document path, is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING the right duplicate behaviour, or should re-posting a plan document UPDATE the matching planned row? The primitive currently uses ignoreDuplicates, so an existing row is left exactly as it is.
best_guess: DO NOTHING. A planned row that has since been dispatched must not be reset to status 'pending' by a second read of the plan it came from, and CR-002's append-only posture points the same way. i3 owns the plan-document path and can read back the skipped set by (engagement_id, plan_ref) if it needs to report on it.

question: The shared registry Field component rendered its 'required' badge inside the <label>, so every required control in this product announced as 'Clientrequired' / 'Engagementrequired'. u2 added aria-hidden to that span in src/app/registry/_components/field.tsx, which changes /registry/new and /registry/[slug]/edit as well as this unit's screen. Reported explicitly rather than folded in silently.

section: CR-005 §3.3 FR-96c — an unresolvable filter renders nothing, loudly
question: An `?engagement=` value longer than 128 characters cannot name any engagement. On the seven screens with a filter bar it lands in the existing `RejectedFilters` banner, which states in words that the list below is NOT narrowed by it and then shows the unfiltered list; on the four screens with no filter bar (`/questions`, `/waits`, `/runs`, `/registry`) u3 routed it to FR-96c's 'no such engagement' state with no rows. section: CR-005 §3.3 FR-96 — which surfaces the filter narrows on /waits
question: On `/waits` under an engagement filter, should the FR-32 declare-a-wait dialog's engagement dropdown also be narrowed to the filtered engagement, or keep offering every engagement?
best_guess: Keep offering every engagement. FR-96 scopes what is SHOWN; narrowing a create control would mean a filtered screen can only record a wait against one client and the operator has to clear a filter to type something, which makes the filter a mode rather than a view. Asserted by test so the choice is visible rather than incidental.

section: advisors / standing repo rule: per-name REVOKE
question: public.rls_auto_enable() is EXECUTE-able by anon AND authenticated as a SECURITY DEFINER function, reachable at /rest/v1/rpc/rls_auto_enable. Two WARN advisors name it. Its proacl reads '=X/postgres || postgres=X || anon=X || authenticated=X || service_role=X' — the leading '=X' is a live grant to PUBLIC. This violates the repo's standing rule that every function in schema public carries a per-name REVOKE FROM public. Should a follow-up unit revoke it, and does anything call it as an RPC?
best_guess: Revoke it. The function is an event-trigger handler that forces RLS on new public tables; it is invoked by the event trigger, not by a client, so no application path should lose anything. It is PRE-EXISTING (created in 20260819144540_rls_and_grants.sql on 2026-08-19) and NOT introduced by i1's migration, so d1 did not touch it — changing grants is a schema write and this unit is verify-only.
confidence: high that it is pre-existing and out of this unit's scope; medium that revoking is safe without reading every caller

question: Supabase advisor reports leaked-password protection (HaveIBeenPwned check) is disabled, level WARN. Spec 7a says 'password policy provider default'. Is provider default the intended posture, or should this be enabled?
best_guess: Compliant as written — 7a explicitly defers the password policy to the provider default, and this is a provider default. Flagged rather than treated as a defect. Enabling it is a dashboard action and therefore Erik's, not an agent's.

question: app.rate_limit_counters has RLS enabled with zero policies (INFO advisor) and has no row in spec 7a, whose roster covers the 21 public tables. Does it need a 7a row, or is schema app deliberately outside the roster?
best_guess: Outside the roster by design: 7a enumerates product entities in schema public, and app is the helper schema. It is unreachable via PostgREST (only exposed schemas are), and RLS-on with no policy denies all non-superuser access, which is the safe direction. Pre-existing, not created by i1. Not treated as the 'entity with no row in 7a is a blocker' case, because that rule is scoped to tables this migration created — i1 created none.

question: Branch agent-build/2026-08-24-d4000f is not pushed to origin, so Vercel Git integration has created no preview deployment for it and there is no preview URL to report. d1 declined to run 'vercel deploy' from the worktree to manufacture one. best_guess: The orchestrator. A CLI deploy from an unpushed worktree would create a deployment with no git metadata, which is not 'the preview deploy for this branch' and would muddy the record; it would also deploy code that has not passed the run's gates. Reported as none-exists with the cause, rather than fabricated.

question: Migration 20260824110601 is applied to the LIVE Supabase project onpvolboecjpdkvurjaf, but the code that uses it (commit 7be6949) is on no remote branch and in no deployment. Production serves e3de4be, built before the migration existed. Is this migrate-first-then-deploy ordering intended for M2.9, and is it acceptable for production to run against a schema it was not built against?
best_guess: Intended and currently safe. Every change is additive or widening: execution_mode dropped NOT NULL (all 20 rows still non-null), four columns added with defaults, one BEFORE UPDATE trigger, one unique index over all-NULL keys under NULLS DISTINCT, and one CHECK that only bites plan_reconciliation='keyed', which nothing writes. Production reads work_item through explicit column lists — the only select("*") in the tree is inside a comment saying it is not used — and the project imports no zod, so no strict schema rejects the four new columns. Production root observed 200 after the migration.
confidence: high on the additive analysis; medium that no unobserved read path is affected, since no agent-token positive path is verifiable this run

question: My worktree HEAD was e3de4be (a merge commit on origin/master), not the 75f070a the brief predicted, so the `git log agent-build/2026-08-24-d4000f..HEAD` precondition printed a line and the brief said to STOP. Was stopping intended for a commit that is provably preserved elsewhere?
best_guess: Proceeded with the reset. `git branch -a --contains e3de4be` showed it on remotes/origin/master, so the reset destroyed no unique work — the precondition exists to prevent losing work, and there was none to lose. Reported both SHAs.

question: The `unparsed` execution-mode sentinel is read-path only and has no Postgres label, unlike `work_status.unparsed` which is a real enum member. Should a later migration add `unparsed` to the `execution_mode` enum so the two closed sets are symmetric?
best_guess: No migration. The sentinel is deliberately unwritable: `EXECUTION_MODES` (the ingest wire vocabulary) excludes it so `validateWorkItem` refuses it from an artifact, and `toExecutionMode` answers null so it cannot be written. A NULL column already means 'no mode', and adding an enum label would give the same fact two spellings in the database.

question: Should `/work-items`'s mode filter gain a `planned` option (i.e. `execution_mode IS NULL`), so Erik can list only planned work?
best_guess: Not built. FR-87 and FR-91 ask for planned work to be visibly *distinguishable*, not filterable, and the filter bar's options are derived from EXECUTION_MODE_LABELS which is deliberately the three writable modes. Adding it needs a PostgREST `.is('execution_mode', null)` branch in listWorkItems and a wire spelling that is not an enum member — a real design decision, not a widening.

question: STALE borrows `--state-contested` (orange). Is reusing a defect-status token for a work-item lifecycle state acceptable, or should Q15's STALE get a seventeenth token at the next palette review?
best_guess: Borrowed `--state-contested`. The brief forbade a new accent or state colour and forbade fuchsia, and contested is the only warm token in the sixteen that never renders on a work-item row — so no work-item column shows one hue for two meanings. Amber was rejected because `carried` is amber and DispositionChip can draw it in the same row.

question: The populated visual sweep could not be done: a git worktree carries only committed content, `.env*.local` is gitignored, so no Supabase credentials are reachable and every screen renders the operator sign-in gate.
best_guess: Reported NOT VERIFIED with the reason. Substituted jsdom renders of the real screens (WorkItemTable with a planned row) so the B43/B46 'component nothing ever mounts' class is covered by a test rather than by a look. Served the production build on :3999 and confirmed every surface answers 200 rather than 500, then killed it and confirmed the port dead.

question: Should a planned row created from a plan document carry `work_item.unit`, and if so what? The plan's only per-task handle is the positional `### Task N:` heading, which shifts the moment a task is inserted.
best_guess: Write `unit = null`. A positional number in a column named `unit` would look like a stable key and is not one — the same hazard Q13 rules against for the reconciliation key, arriving through a different column. `plan_ref` is the only key this path writes.

section: CR-005 §3.1a FR-90 — where a reconciliation is attempted
question: FR-90's trigger is 'an ingested run reports a work unit that a planned row already describes'. That meeting can happen in either order — plan first then run, or run first then plan. Should the collision mark be written on BOTH paths, or only when a plan document is ingested?
best_guess: Both. I mark on the plan-document path and also after `persistPlan` in `POST /api/ingest/run`, through one shared function. Marking on only one path leaves a real collision unmarked whenever the run lands second, and the mark's stated meaning ('a reconciliation was attempted and no key existed') is true in both orders. This needs no change to `persist.ts` — `persistPlan` already returns `engagementId`.

section: CR-005 §3.1 FR-89 — plan tasks the parser did not classify
question: A `### Task` heading that i2's parser emits as `status: unparsed` has `title: null`. Should it become a planned row anyway (description from the raw heading), or be withheld?
best_guess: Withheld and counted, never written. u2's primitive fixes `status = 'pending'`, so writing an unparsed task would assert this product understood a line it did not — a wrong `done`. The response reports the count and the source line numbers so nothing is dropped in silence.

question: A plan task carries `- [ ]` steps. §7a models no child entity under `work_item`, so should step texts be folded into the planned row's description, dropped, or persisted somewhere?
best_guess: Not persisted in M2.9, and the count reported. One planned row per Task; the steps stay in the plan document. Folding them into `description` makes a paragraph out of a one-line answer to 'what is next', and §7a has no entity for them.

section: spec §7a — agent capability for the plan route
question: Should `POST /api/ingest/plan` require a new capability (e.g. `plan:write`) rather than reusing `ingest:write`?
best_guess: Reuse `ingest:write`. It grants no new authority: a token holding `ingest:write` can already insert `work_item` rows through `POST /api/ingest/run`, and this route writes the same table under the same §7a class. A new capability would need a new member of the stored capability enum — a migration this unit was told it should not need. Flagged rather than assumed because it is a capability boundary.

section: CR-005 §3.1 FR-89 — a document that is not a plan
question: Q12 says a document not of the plan shape is 'rejected whole'. Is that a 400 to the caller, or a 200 carrying the rejection reason and zero rows?
best_guess: 400 `invalid_request`, naming i2's `NotAPlanReason`. The caller posted something this endpoint cannot act on, and a 200 reporting zero rows written is the quiet answer this product exists to stop being given.

section: FR-96b — the engagement picker's not-in-the-active-list option (engagement-scope.tsx:245)
question: u1 asked for a shorter wording because `w-36` truncates the option; measured in the served build the shipped string renders 216px into a 144px box, and no wording fits — the slug alone is 108px for `delivery-ledger`, so for a realistic slug the closed picker shows the slug and nothing else, reading as an ordinary selection. The screen below renders FR-96c's explicit notice, which is the required and unmissable signal; the picker is secondary, and shortening to `not listed` (129.6px) still overflows for a realistic slug while dropping the word `active` that explains why it is absent. Measurement handed to u1/qa1 as a layout question.

question: `unknown` and `fresh` render the identical word `planned`, and are told apart only by the age token (`age?` versus `12d`) and by a dotted rather than dashed 1px border. question: The 34 committed .txt page transcripts under .fleet/manual-traces/ hold full rendered page text from a populated instance, which includes decrypted work_item descriptions, defect prose and client names. Only the .png files are gitignored (.gitignore line 36). Should the .txt transcripts be gitignored and purged from history, or is committing them accepted for this repo?

question: docs/user-guide.md names the engagement slug `delivery-ledger` in three places, written by run 29b583. §7a classes `engagement.client_name` as personal and this unit's brief forbids a real engagement slug in the guide. Should a seeded instance (or a scratch engagement that is later purged) exist so the manual can verify hand-entry and the staleness treatment end to end?

question: manual-gate.sh checks that every served route has an evidence row with an observation, but it cannot tell a fresh observation from a stale one copied forward. It would have passed this run with all 30 rows carried verbatim, including /runs' now-false claim that no engagement filter exists. Should the evidence schema carry a per-row observed-on commit or date the gate can compare against the branch tip?
best_guess: Yes — a per-row `observed_at_commit`, failing when it is an ancestor of the tip and the route's page files changed since. That closes the one false-green this gate is structurally open to.

question: Should `.fleet/manual-traces/*.txt` gain an explicit §7a row classifying it `internal` for the `delivery-ledger` engagement only, rather than being purged from history?
best_guess: Yes. The only slug in all 34 committed files is `delivery-ledger` (272 occurrences) — Erik's own repo, no third-party client, no token shapes. A history purge plus force-push to origin/master is disproportionate; a §7a line plus a pre-commit gate refusing any other engagement slug is the proportionate control.

question: Should the FR-90 failure inside POST /api/ingest/run degrade to a 200 carrying `reconciliation: {failed: true}` instead of throwing a 500 after `persistPlan` has committed?
best_guess: Yes. The run is already persisted and the marking is idempotent and re-runnable, so a 500 misreports the outcome and invites a redundant re-post. At minimum the message must stop saying 'Nothing else was changed', which is affirmatively false.

question: When FR-90's write half lands, should `plan_reconciliation = 'collision'` keep its current meaning — every unreconciled planned row in an engagement that holds any ingested row — or narrow to rows with an actual counterpart?
best_guess: Narrow it then, not now. Today the broad mark is conservative and correct under Q13, but it approximates 'this engagement has both kinds of row'. Once a shared key exists the mark can mean what its name says, and the broad form should not be inherited by default.

question: Should a test enumerate `src/app/api/**/route.ts` and assert every exported handler is guarded, with `/api/export` listed by mechanism (requireOperator) rather than exempted?
best_guess: Yes. All 14 handlers are guarded today by convention only, and a naive grep already misled project-lead once about `/api/export`. Listing the mechanism per route makes the exception legible instead of looking like a hole.

question: Is `text-muted-foreground/70` at `text-xs` (measured 3.55:1, AA needs 4.5:1) an accepted deviation, or should the token be fixed repo-wide?
best_guess: Fix repo-wide as its own small milestone. It is pre-existing across 10+ files (96 nodes on /questions), and this run added two more instances including FR-91's own chip; a single token change closes all of them at once.

question: Should `aria-sort` move from the sort `<a>` to the enclosing `<th>` in the three tables that set it?
best_guess: Yes. axe rates it critical (aria-allowed-attr, 7 nodes); `aria-sort` is only valid on columnheader/rowheader, so sort state is currently announced to nobody. Pre-existing, but this run edited all three files.

question: Should the specialist contract require an api-integrator to read the migration or generated types directly before writing a query, rather than accepting an upstream unit's report as the schema?
best_guess: Yes. i4 wrote a correct query having read only i1's report and the consuming code — right answer, unverified route, and it breaks silently the next time the column list moves. A one-line contract clause naming the migration or database.types.ts closes it.

question: Should a red-capable proof performed post-hoc by mutation be reported as such, rather than as 'proved red first'?
best_guess: Yes. c1's proof was real, restored, and epistemically sound, but its report says 'first' and the trace shows last. Both orders are acceptable engineering; only one of them is what happened, and on this project the ordering of a red proof is exactly what gets claimed rather than done.

question: Should `manual-gate.sh` record a content hash plus observing run id per route and refuse evidence whose run id is not the current one?
best_guess: Yes. It currently cannot distinguish a fresh observation from a copied one, and doc1 found two shipped-guide claims this milestone falsified that a copy-forward would have preserved under a green gate. As it stands the gate certifies that a file exists.

question: Should CR-005 §4's 'nullable columns' wording be amended to match the schema, which landed three of four new columns `not null` with defaults?
best_guess: Amend the CR. The defaults mean nothing broke and no write path must supply them, so the schema is right and the wording is stale; leaving them in disagreement invites a future reviewer to file it as a defect.

question: Should a scoped, expiring agent token be exported into the review shell's environment so a future qa pass can prove the token boundary ADMITS, not only that it refuses?
best_guess: Yes, if Erik wants positive-path coverage — but it must be a minted per-run token in the environment, never a relaxation of the .claude/settings.json denial on .env.local. Today every agent-token positive claim across the fleet is unverified by construction.

section: QA d4000f important #1 / FR-58 / POST /api/ingest/run response contract
question: When the run commits but FR-90 collision marking fails, should the route answer 200 with a `reconciliation.failed` marker (preserving `persisted`, `fleetRunId` and FR-58's `unparsed` count) instead of the current 500, which discards all of them?
best_guess: Keep the 500 and correct only the sentence, which is exactly what QA prescribed and is the narrower change. Noting that the 500 path still withholds FR-58's unparsed count after a successful persist — a contract question for Erik, not a worktree decision.

question: `markPlanCollisions` is shared by POST /api/ingest/run and POST /api/ingest/plan, so QA's suggested wording 'The run was persisted' would be false on the plan path. Is caller-agnostic wording acceptable, or should each caller pass in what it committed?
best_guess: Caller-agnostic wording ('Everything this request wrote before this step stands and was not rolled back'), because it is true in both directions and needs no signature change and no edit to the plan path.

section: src/lib/api/errors.ts toErrorResponse — adjacent, deliberately not fixed
question: An unexpected non-ApiError thrown after `persistPlan` commits still reaches the caller as the generic 'The request could not be completed.', which is the same wrong 'not done' shape QA raised. Out of this unit's scope and unraised by QA — should it be addressed separately?
best_guess: Leave it. I catch nothing extra in this unit; only the ApiError path QA named is changed. Flagging rather than widening.
